program_overview.title: App Development for Teens
program_overview.tagline: The phone in their pocket becomes the thing they build for: real apps, installed on real devices, shipped with one honest stack in ten months.
program_overview.description:
Every teenager lives inside apps; very few know they could build one this year. This live online course takes students aged 13 to 18 from zero to a real, installable, launched mobile app, using the path the modern industry actually recommends for one-person teams: JavaScript learned properly, React for interface thinking, then React Native with Expo, one codebase that runs on both Android and iOS, with Firebase as the backend and AI features where they genuinely help.

The stack choice is the honest part. Courses that tour four frameworks, Kotlin, Swift, React Native and Flutter, produce teens fluent in none of them. This course masters one: React Native powers apps at Meta, Microsoft, Shopify and thousands of startups, works fully on a Windows laptop, and lets a teen carry their JavaScript skills from web to phone. Flutter gets an honest taste week, and native Android and iOS get a clear map, what they are, when they matter, and where our Kotlin and Swift courses continue.

The pace is real: ten months at two live classes a week plus three to four hours of practice, with two more months in hand when needed. Apps go onto real phones from month 3, the capstone is user-tested and distributed properly, and store publishing is explained exactly as it works for minors: developer accounts are parent-managed, and we walk families through it. Homework after every class, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest. Real apps, real users, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: One stack mastered, honestly chosen: JavaScript, React and React Native with Expo, the one-person-team path the industry actually uses
Runs on any laptop: no Mac required for the course; iOS specifics and Apple’s rules are explained honestly
Apps on real phones from month 3: Expo puts student work on their own device almost immediately
Store truth for minors: developer accounts are parent-managed and we walk families through exactly how distribution works
AI features built in properly: server-side calls, streaming and guardrails inside the student’s own app
Real assessment: weekly homework, mixed-review assignments every month, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest

faqs.question: What will my teen build in this app development course?
faqs.answer: More than 20 real builds across ten months, on an escalating ladder: an installable web app in month 2, a first React Native app on their own phone in month 3, an offline-capable app with camera and location features, a polished beta-tested app with an AI feature by month 6, a one-week micro-app sprint, and finally a capstone app that is spec’d, built, beta-tested, distributed and launched to real users, then presented at demo day.

faqs.question: How long does it take a teenager to learn app development?
faqs.answer: To a genuinely launched app: 10 months at 2 live classes a week plus 3 to 4 hours of practice. The syllabus keeps 2 months of margin in hand, students who need more repetition take up to 12 months with no rushing and no penalty. The first app lands on their own phone in month 3, so motivation never has to wait for the finish line.

faqs.question: How is my teen assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Classwork runs inside every session, homework follows every class, and each month ends with an assignment that deliberately mixes new questions with earlier topics so knowledge compounds instead of fading. Every phase closes with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions drawn from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns a focused revision plan and a free retest.

faqs.question: Why React Native instead of Kotlin, Swift or Flutter?
faqs.answer: Because one stack mastered beats four toured, and React Native is the honest choice for a one-person teen team: one codebase for Android and iOS, full development on a Windows laptop, JavaScript skills that transfer to and from the web, and real industry weight behind it. The course still gives Flutter an honest taste week and maps native Kotlin and Swift clearly, and our dedicated Kotlin and Swift courses continue those roads for students who want native depth.

faqs.question: Do we need a Mac or an iPhone?
faqs.answer: No Mac is needed for the course: React Native with Expo runs fully on Windows, and cloud build services handle iOS packaging when needed. Any Android or iOS phone works for testing. The Apple publishing path, its account, cost and review process, is explained honestly in the store-readiness week for families who want to pursue it.

faqs.question: Will my teen actually publish an app to the stores?
faqs.answer: Here is the straight answer most courses avoid: store developer accounts have age and payment requirements, so for minors they are parent-managed, and we walk families through exactly that in the distribution weeks. Every student ships for real regardless: internal testing tracks, direct installs and PWA distribution put the capstone in real users’ hands, and families who set up a parent-managed account can take it all the way to a public store listing.

faqs.question: How is AI used in this course?
faqs.answer: Two ways, both honest. Students build AI features into their own apps, model calls made safely, streaming responses, guardrails against misuse, with accounts set up with a parent where a service requires it. And they learn to use AI coding assistants the professional way: as accelerators for a developer who understands the code, never as a substitute for understanding it.
